papers.title: Schwarzschild scattering from CFT
papers.abstract: We show that retarded CFT correlators on $\mathbb{R}\times \mathbb{S}^2$ in a state described by the small black hole in AdS$_4$ can be used to derive asymptotically flat Schwarzschild partial-wave S-matrix elements, including its spectrum of quasinormal modes. This is achieved by identifying a class of operators for which the dual bulk fields behave as plane waves near the AdS boundary for sufficiently high frequencies. For such operators there is a simple analytic relation between CFT correlators and reflection coefficients which behaves gracefully in the flat space limit, $L\to \infty$. These include spin-1, spin-2, and conformally coupled scalars. We provide a simple toy model that captures how dissipative QNMs can appear for short times inside Hermitian systems, closely resembling the small black hole in AdS.
papers.summary: This work shows how retarded CFT correlators on $mathbb{R}	imesmathbb{S}^2$ in a small AdS$_4$ black hole state can be mapped to asymptotically flat Schwarzschild scattering amplitudes, including the quasinormal mode spectrum. By identifying operators whose bulk duals become plane waves at high frequency, the authors derive a simple analytic relation between CFT correlators and flat‑space reflection coefficients, offering a toy model for dissipative QNMs in Hermitian systems.

papers.title: Gravitational Memory Correlators and BMS Symmetry
papers.authors: Enrico Herrmann, Ian Moult, Brett Oertel, Julio Parra-Martinez, Biswajit Sahoo
papers.abstract: We compute the n-point memory and mixed energy-memory correlators for scalar decay into gravitons using the in-in formalism at leading order in perturbative quantum gravity. We obtain compact results for arbitrary n and explicitly verify the supertranslation flux balance relation between memory, energy, and Bondi mass detectors, realizing asymptotic symmetry constraints on infrared-finite observables.
papers.summary: The authors compute n‑point memory and mixed energy‑memory correlators for scalar decay into gravitons using the in‑in formalism, obtaining compact expressions that satisfy the supertranslation flux‑balance relation. Their results provide explicit checks of BMS symmetry constraints on infrared‑finite observables, offering new tools for studying asymptotic symmetries in quantum gravity.

papers.title: Rational conformal interfaces between the Ising and tricritical Ising models from a tetrality web
papers.authors: Ant\'onio Antunes, Jin Chen, Junchen Rong
papers.abstract: We construct rational conformal interfaces between the Ising and tricritical Ising (TIM) models by using different chiral symmetries to prepare their folded boundary states. We use a moving up procedure which extends the product theory to an auxiliary coset with an $S_3$ automorphism group, where permutations give twisted Cardy states. We complement this with a moving down approach which reduces to the $S_3$ invariant algebra. Overall, these procedures uncover a tetrality web relating four different theories. Pulling back ordinary Cardy states of the smallest theory in the web to the physical tensor product system gives eighteen factorized interfaces and six transmitting interfaces. The latter agree with four transposition and two 3-cycle twisted boundaries in the largest theory. They include Gaiotto's RG wall and the interface obtained by fusing an Ising duality line into it. The six interfaces carry the regular action of the TIM fusion ring and have the same energy transmission coefficient, $35/48$. Their boundary entropies, bulk correlations and operator spectra distinguish them. We calculate these observables and the complete annulus amplitudes between the twenty four boundaries.
papers.summary: The paper constructs rational conformal interfaces between the Ising and tricritical Ising models using chiral symmetries and an auxiliary coset with an (S_3) automorphism, revealing a tetrality web of four related theories. It identifies eighteen factorized and six transmitting interfaces—including Gaiotto’s RG wall—computes their boundary entropies, bulk correlations, and annulus amplitudes, and shows they all share the same energy transmission coefficient.

papers.title: Constants and Nonperturbative Corrections in $V^{5,2}$ Theories
papers.abstract: We study perturbative and exponentially small corrections to the on-shell effective twisted superpotentials of two three-dimensional $\mathcal N=2$ theories associated with free and fixed-locus cyclic quotients of the non-toric Sasaki-Einstein manifold $V^{5,2}$. These are the two-node Chern-Simons theory at levels $(k,-k)$ and the one-node flavored theory with $N_f$ fundamental pairs, respectively. At superconformal chemical potentials, we propose the Chern-Simons counterpart of the all-order perturbative expression for the flavored theory and obtain convergent integral representations for the rank-independent constants of both theories. At integer parameters, these constants admit explicit evaluations involving finite sums of Clausen functions and $\zeta(3)$, while their large-parameter expansions Borel sum to the defining integrals. At $k=1,3$ and $N_f=1,3$, we conjecture complete exponential remainders expressed through Eichler integrals of weight-four Eisenstein series. Supported by high-precision Bethe solutions, the resulting completions coincide at unit quotient order but differ at order three. We determine the minimal modular levels of the Eisenstein generators and establish convergence and natural boundaries for their primitives. Within the relative M-theory localization prescription, a complementary bulk analysis recovers the Chern-Simons shifted rank and constant in the $b\to0^+$ limit of the squashed-sphere partition function. We propose a generalization incorporating fixed-locus contributions that yields the corresponding flavored-theory result. The two theories therefore share a modular structure in their nonperturbative coefficient laws, but distinct perturbative shifts and exponential corrections resolve differences invisible in their common leading $N^{3/2}$ behavior.
papers.summary: We analyze perturbative and exponentially suppressed corrections to the twisted superpotentials of two 3d $mathcal N=2$ Chern‑Simons–type theories on the Sasaki‑Einstein manifold $V^{5,2}$, uncovering a modular structure governed by Eisenstein series and Borel‑summable integrals that encode rank‑independent constants. The work connects M‑theory localization, shifted ranks, and non‑perturbative completions, revealing distinct exponential remainders while preserving the universal $N^{3/2}$ scaling.

papers.title: Quadratic Sum Rules for Scalar Amplitudes
papers.authors: Karol Kampf, Ji\v{r}\'i Novotn\'y, David Podiv\'in, Jonah Stalknecht
papers.abstract: Kleiss--Kuijf and Bern--Carrasco--Johansson relations, and their string monodromy generalizations, have long provided some of the most powerful and useful constraints on partial amplitudes. Motivated by their success, we uncover a new class of quadratic-sum rules that connect scalar amplitudes at different multiplicities. Combining recursion, kinematic shifts, and symbolic regression, we establish them for the nonlinear sigma model and its string-inspired extensions. We then extend these relations to diagonal elements of the inverse Kawai--Lewellen--Tye matrix and subsequently to planar scalar theories with nonderivative interactions and general propagators.
papers.summary: The authors derive new quadratic-sum rules linking scalar amplitudes of different multiplicities, extending BCJ/KLT relations via recursion, kinematic shifts, and symbolic regression in the nonlinear sigma model and its string-inspired variants. These relations also generalize to inverse KLT matrices and planar scalar theories with arbitrary propagators, offering new algebraic constraints on multi-point scattering amplitudes.

papers.title: Generalised global symmetries of 6d SCFTs on a circle from the blow-up equations
papers.abstract: We study 6d $(1,0)$ SCFTs on a circle, possibly twisted, through the blow-up equations of their 5d descriptions. For every theory we consider, we construct the explicit map between the 6d and 5d frames, including the ratio $r$ of the Kaluza--Klein (KK) mass to the instanton mass, which depends on the frame and not only on the twist. Our main result is that the higher-form symmetries of these theories, their mixed anomalies and 2-groups can all be read off from the fluxes through the exceptional curve of the blown-up $\mathbb{C}^2$. The flux sectors are the 't$~$Hooft sectors of the 5d 1-form symmetries. On the tensor fluxes, the 6d Green--Schwarz couplings fix the weights, whose fractional exponents we read as the mixed anomalies of the 6d 2-form symmetry with the KK $\mathrm{U}(1)$, gravity, flavour and $\mathrm{SU}(2)_R$. The fluxes forced in each sector decide between a 2-group and a mixed anomaly. For instance, the twisted frames $\mathfrak{su}(4)_{0,4}+4\Lambda^2$ carry a non-split $\mathbb{Z}_4$ 2-group, while, in $\mathfrak{su}(4)_2+4\Lambda^2$ and $\mathfrak{su}(4)_6+2\Lambda^2$, the instanton symmetry is locked to the flavour centre and only a mixed anomaly remains. The same method applies to the $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ gauging of two, three and four copies of the $E_1$ theory, which describes, respectively, $\mathrm{SU}(4)_0$, pure $\mathrm{Spin}(8)$ and the untwisted $\mathfrak{so}(8)$ KK theory. There, the fluxes exhibit the extensions of 1-form symmetries inherited from the $E_1$ 2-groups, identify the states that break each accidental 1-form symmetry and the background to which it is locked, and give the 5d 2-group to which the $S_3$-invariant 6d 3-group reduces.
papers.summary: The paper develops a systematic method to extract the higher‑form symmetry structure and mixed anomalies of 6d (1,0) SCFTs compactified on a circle by analyzing the blow‑up equations of their 5d gauge theory descriptions. By mapping flux sectors on the exceptional curve to ’t Hooft sectors, the authors determine 2‑group extensions, mixed anomalies with KK U(1), gravity, flavor, and SU(2)_R, and illustrate the method on several SU(4) and SO(8) examples.

papers.title: Non-Topological Chiral Anomaly: The Chiral Magnetoelectric Effect
papers.authors: R\'emy Larue, Amaury Marchon, J\'er\'emie Quevillon, Diego Saviot
papers.abstract: We derive the chiral anomaly in a thermal medium and show that, in addition to the well-established topological piece, the anomaly acquires a previously overlooked non-topological contribution, relevant for non-gauged axial symmetries. Remarkably, this modification of the continuity equation is independent of the electromagnetic fields, thereby giving rise to novel transport effects in relativistic hydrodynamics. We further propose an experimentally accessible new effect in Weyl semimetals which we call the Chiral Magnetoelectric Effect: an electric field proportional to the magnetic field is generated by the non-topological anomaly, even in the absence of an externally applied electric field. Beyond this concrete prediction, our results establish a broader hydrodynamic framework for non-topological chiral anomalies, opening the door to a range of previously unexplored anomaly-induced transport phenomena across condensed-matter and high-energy systems.
papers.summary: The paper derives a non-topological contribution to the chiral anomaly in thermal media, leading to a novel chiral magnetoelectric effect in Weyl semimetals. It extends hydrodynamic anomaly frameworks but offers little overlap with the physicist’s interests.

papers.title: A Bound on Wormhole Probing Time from Holographic Multi-Entropy
papers.abstract: Bipartite entanglement entropy eventually saturates and therefore cannot track the continued growth of an eternal wormhole. Recently, it was shown that genuine tripartite multi-entropy can probe wormhole growth even after bipartite entanglement entropies have saturated. This naturally raises the question: can increasing the number of parties extend the probing time indefinitely? Adopting the multiway maximin prescription and assuming that its selected representatives are regular spacetime-stationary networks, we prove that the answer is no for nonrotating BTZ black holes. We establish a common finite upper bound on the probing time for every fixed finite boundary partition, independent of the number, sizes, and arrangement of its parties. For any network on any Cauchy slice, there exists a comparison network that assigns the entire central region containing the wormhole interior to a single party. A network longer than this comparison network cannot minimize length on that slice. The central length required by a stationary network connecting the two boundaries grows with time, whereas the central length of the comparison network remains uniformly bounded. At sufficiently late times, such a network therefore cannot minimize length on any Cauchy slice containing it and is excluded from the maximin prescription. Consequently, beyond this bound, no network selected by maximin enters the black-hole interior.
papers.summary: The paper proves that for nonrotating BTZ black holes, the time during which multi‑party entanglement entropies can probe the wormhole interior is bounded independently of the number of parties. Using a multiway maximin construction, it shows that beyond a finite time no stationary network can enter the black‑hole interior, thus limiting the probing time for any finite boundary partition.

papers.title: Projected DKP spin-1 sectors in a $(2+1)$-dimensional static wormhole: Self-duality, helicity content, and spectral correspondence
papers.abstract: We use the projected spin-1 Duffin--Kemmer--Petiau (DKP) equation in $2+1$ dimensions to clarify the physical content of the irreducible $3\times3$ representations. The projected antisymmetric tensor is algebraically dual to the projected vector, and the two twin representations select conjugate self-dual covariant-curl sectors, which reduce to opposite massive helicities in the flat-space limit. We then apply this structure to the static wormhole problem previously studied with a single irreducible representation. The first-order radial DKP system contains an exceptional normalizable bound-state branch at $\omega^2=M^2$ that is absent from the master-variable reduction, whereas the generic master and circular sectors are related by a Darboux transformation. The latter preserves the transmission and reflection probabilities, while the quasinormal modes are organized into two pole families in the complex radial-momentum plane, leading to the physical pairing $(\omega,-\omega^*)$ rather than a global $\pm\omega$ prescription.
papers.summary: The paper analyzes the projected spin‑1 DKP equation in 2+1 dimensions, revealing a duality between antisymmetric tensor and vector representations that yields opposite massive helicities in flat space. It then applies this structure to a static wormhole, uncovering an exceptional bound‑state branch and a Darboux‑related spectral correspondence that organizes quasinormal modes into conjugate pole families.

papers.title: Stochastic gauge fixing from the holographic renormalization group
papers.abstract: We extend the dictionary between stochastic quantization and holographic Wilsonian renormalization to Yang-Mills theory in four-dimensional anti-de Sitter space at tree level. The radial component of the bulk gauge field is Zwanziger's gauge-fixing function; radial gauge is Parisi-Wu quantization, whose random walk of gauge modes is the longitudinal bulk propagator. We obtain the triple- and quadruple-trace couplings of gluons at finite cutoff in closed form. On transverse data, their dependence on the bulk gauge resides in a single zero mode, which drops out of the flat-space limit.
papers.summary: This work extends the stochastic quantization–holographic Wilsonian RG dictionary to Yang–Mills theory in AdS4, identifying the radial bulk gauge component as Zwanziger’s gauge-fixing function and deriving closed-form triple- and quadruple-trace gluon couplings at finite cutoff. The analysis shows that transverse data depend on the bulk gauge only through a single zero mode, which vanishes in the flat-space limit, offering new insights into gauge dynamics in holographic settings.

papers.title: Conditional Principle of Least Action: Gauge Algebra and Noether's Second Theorem
papers.authors: V. A. Abakumova, S. L. Lyakhovich
papers.abstract: We consider the problem of a conditional extremum of an action within a class of fields constrained by differential equations. For this setup, we establish the interconnection between the gauge symmetry algebra of the equations constraining the admissible fields and that of the action restricted to this class of fields. Based on this relation between the two gauge algebras, we derive an extension of Noether's second theorem and its converse. The general method is illustrated by the example of linearized gravity with the Einstein-Hilbert action and the class of admissible metrics restricted by the Cotton equation.
papers.summary: This paper extends Noether’s second theorem to actions constrained by differential equations, linking the gauge algebra of the constraints to that of the restricted action. It illustrates the result with linearized gravity, showing how the Cotton equation restricts the Einstein–Hilbert action.

papers.title: Classification of Conformal Ising/Tricritical Ising Interfaces Preserving $\mathcal{W}_3^{\mathbb{Z}_2}$ Symmetry
papers.abstract: We classify conformal interfaces between the Ising and tricritical Ising models that preserve the chiral algebra $\mathcal{W}_3^{\mathbb{Z}_2}$. Using the folding trick, we formulate the problem in terms of boundary states satisfying the Cardy condition and determine the unique NIM-rep compatible with the bulk partition function. We obtain a complete set of 24 fundamental boundary states, of which 18 correspond to factorized interfaces preserving the full product Virasoro symmetry, while the remaining six break this symmetry. We construct these six interfaces explicitly and determine their annulus partition functions. They are related by topological defect line dressings, and one coincides with the RG domain wall proposed by Gaiotto.
papers.summary: The authors classify all conformal interfaces between the Ising and tricritical Ising minimal models that preserve the $mathcal{W}_3^{mathbb{Z}_2}$ chiral algebra. They find 24 fundamental boundary states, 18 of which are factorized and 6 break the product Virasoro symmetry, and construct the latter explicitly, including the RG domain wall of Gaiotto.

papers.title: Large-$N$ expansion in SU($N$) Yang-Mills-like theories
papers.authors: Marco Bochicchio, Mauro Papinutto, Francesco Scardino
papers.abstract: It has been known for fifty years that bare U($N$) pure Yang-Mills (YM) theory admits the large-$N$ 't Hooft expansion for the $n$-point connected correlators of gauge-invariant single-trace operators, where the corresponding Feynman diagrams are topologically classified by the sum over the genus $g$ of $n$-punctured smooth orientable closed Riemann surfaces. In fact, 't Hooft expansion extends verbatim to U($N$) YM-like theories whose Lagrangians only involve fields valued in the U($N$) Lie algebra - including supersymmetric (SUSY) extensions of pure YM theory such as $\mathcal{N}=1,4$ SUSY YM. The aim of the present paper is to systematically work out the topology of the large-$N$ expansion in SU($N$) - as opposed to U($N$) - YM-like theories, where a number of subtleties inevitably arise. Indeed, since the U($1$) inside the U($N$) YM-like theories decouples, the large-$N$ U($N$) and SU($N$) expansions should either essentially coincide or intrinsically differ - in the latter case necessarily by extra - possibly singular - topologies, as the 't Hooft expansion in U($N$) YM-like theories already exhausts all the smooth topologies. In fact, we demonstrate that 't Hooft smooth topologies are actually generically incomplete in the large-$N$ expansion of both the SU($N$) and renormalized U($N$) YM-like theories, where renormalization inevitably separates the SU($N$) sector that is interacting from the U($1$) sector that is free. Specifically, we interpret the extra topologies that arise in SU($N$) theories for correlators of higher-twist quasi-partonic operators as singular pinched closed surfaces, thus extending our previous investigation of correlators of twist-$2$ operators for which extra pinched tori arise.
papers.summary: This paper extends the classic ’t Hooft large‑N expansion from U(N) to SU(N) Yang‑Mills‑like theories, uncovering new singular pinched‑surface topologies that appear when the decoupled U(1) sector is removed. The authors show that these extra topologies are necessary for a complete description of higher‑twist quasi‑partonic operator correlators, indicating that the smooth Riemann‑surface classification is incomplete for SU(N).

papers.title: The $\mathbb{Z}_2$ twist line defect of the 3D Ising CFT on the fuzzy sphere from multi-target density matrix renormalization group
papers.abstract: The fuzzy-sphere regularization provides a powerful framework for studying three-dimensional (3D) conformal field theories (CFTs) through radial quantization, but conformal defects have so far been studied with it only by exact diagonalization (ED) of small systems. In this work we realize the $\mathbb{Z}_2$ twist line defect of the 3D Ising CFT on the fuzzy sphere by imposing antiperiodic boundary conditions on the $\mathbb{Z}_2$-odd fermion flavor, and solve it with a multi-target density matrix renormalization group (DMRG) algorithm that optimizes several low-lying states of each symmetry sector in a common matrix-product basis. This gives the defect spectrum at system sizes well beyond the reach of ED (up to $2s+1=25$, or $49$ spinless orbitals). The spectrum obeys the spin-parity selection rule of the twist line and organizes into conformal multiplets along the line. Using the displacement operator as an intrinsic ruler, its protected descendant as a test, and the bulk stress tensor as an independent cross-check, we identify the leading finite-size corrections and obtain controlled continuum extrapolations, which sharpen the dimensions of several known defect primaries and resolve four higher-lying ones. This study establishes the fuzzy sphere combined with multi-target DMRG as a framework for precision studies of conformal defects.
papers.summary: The paper develops a fuzzy-sphere regularization combined with multi-target DMRG to compute the spectrum of the $mathbb{Z}_2$ twist line defect in the 3D Ising CFT, achieving system sizes far beyond exact diagonalization and extracting continuum-extrapolated defect operator dimensions. It demonstrates that the defect spectrum organizes into conformal multiplets, with finite-size corrections identified via the displacement operator and bulk stress tensor, thereby establishing a new precision tool for studying conformal defects.

papers.title: Holographic Entanglement after a Global Quench in Noncommutative Yang-Mills Theory
papers.authors: Elahe Hassanpour, Komeil Babaei Velni, M. Reza Mohammadi Mozaffar
papers.abstract: The time evolution of holographic entanglement entropy and mixed-state correlations following a global quench in four-dimensional N=4 noncommutative Yang-Mills theory is investigated using a Vaidya geometry. For strip-shaped regions extended along a noncommutative direction, two distinct early-time growth regimes emerge, depending on the relation between the shell-crossing and noncommutative scales: logarithmic growth, with a coefficient proportional to the injected energy density and the square of the noncommutative scale, followed by quadratic growth. For sufficiently wide strips, an intermediate linear-growth regime appears, governed by an entanglement velocity that increases with noncommutativity. The approach to equilibrium is also examined, revealing the role of the butterfly velocity in the continuous evolution of extremal surfaces, while competing branches can modify the physical saturation time. For two disjoint strips, the leading width-independent logarithmic contribution cancels in the mutual information, whereas the entanglement wedge cross section exhibits an intermediate linear-growth regime governed by the same entanglement velocity, provided the connected entanglement wedge remains dominant.
papers.summary: This work studies the time evolution of holographic entanglement entropy and mixed-state correlations in four-dimensional N=4 noncommutative Yang-Mills following a global quench, uncovering distinct early-time growth regimes (logarithmic, quadratic, and linear) that depend on noncommutativity and strip width. It also analyzes how the entanglement velocity, butterfly velocity, and entanglement wedge cross section govern the approach to equilibrium and the behavior of mutual information for disjoint regions.

papers.title: On the Spontaneous symmetry breaking of Conformal Gravity to Weyl and Einstein Gravities
papers.authors: Partha Nandi, Gerasimos Kouniatalis, Stelios Stefas, George Zoupanos
papers.abstract: Does the special-conformal connection remain an auxiliary field when a spontaneously broken conformal gauge theory is promoted to a fully dynamical Yang-Mills-Higgs theory, and under what conditions does its elimination yield Weyl gravity? We address these questions within an $\mathrm{SO}(2,4)$ gauge-theoretic formulation of gravity. Revisiting the gravitational sector selected by spontaneous symmetry breaking through an adjoint $15$-plet, we retain the special-conformal connection as an independent field and demonstrate that, on a source-free projected branch, its algebraic equation of motion determines it in terms of the Schouten tensor. Eliminating this connection yields the four-dimensional Weyl-squared action, up to the Euler density, without imposing the Schouten relation as an additional geometrical constraint. We then extend the analysis to the standard local Yang-Mills-Higgs theory and show that the special-conformal connection remains auxiliary, owing to the structure of the invariant bilinear form of $\mathfrak{so}(2,4)$, which prevents the appearance of an independent kinetic operator. The additional gauge and scalar sectors can modify its algebraic solution, so the exact Weyl reduction is restricted to the source-free branch. We further investigate the linearised spectrum of the reduced Weyl theory around de Sitter spacetime, identifying massless and partially massless spin-2 branches, with the latter occurring at $m_{\mathrm{PM}}^2=2\Lambda/3$. Finally, we discuss the subsequent symmetry breaking induced by an antisymmetric scalar $6$-plet and its role in connecting the Weyl-gravity phase to Einstein gravity.
papers.summary: This paper studies spontaneous symmetry breaking in an SO(2,4) gauge-theoretic formulation of gravity, showing that the special-conformal connection can be eliminated algebraically to yield the Weyl-squared action on a source-free branch. It further analyzes the linearized spectrum around de Sitter, identifies partially massless spin-2 modes, and discusses how an antisymmetric scalar 6-plet can drive a transition to Einstein gravity.

papers.title: The Goldstone--Wilczek Charge on the Rim
papers.abstract: A solenoid flux $\Phi=2\pi\alpha$ threaded through the center of the Kaplan--Sen lattice disk binds a ground-state charge $Q_{\rm core}=\alpha-\mathrm{round}(\alpha)$, and the edge carries exactly the opposite charge. The edge charge is the Goldstone--Wilczek charge of the edge ladder, $Q_{\rm edge}=-\tfrac12\eta$, with $\eta$ its spectral asymmetry. At $\Phi=\pi$ one unit of charge crosses the disk. We ask how the rim operator, the Schur complement of the disk Hamiltonian on its boundary sites, registers this transfer. Its count of negative eigenvalues never changes over the flux cycle. Instead, the unit of charge enters the rim through a simple pole: the extremal eigenvalue of the rim operator passes through infinity in the same flux interval as the charge jump, with $\Delta Q_{\rm edge}=\tfrac12\Delta\,\mathrm{sign}\,\lambda_{\rm ext}$. The residue factorizes into the coupling of the inner edge mode to the rim and the inverse slope of that mode's level, and grows linearly with the radius. All statements are checked numerically on disks of radius $R=11$, $19$ and $34$.
papers.summary: The paper studies how a magnetic flux through a lattice disk induces a fractional charge on the edge, captured by the spectral asymmetry of the edge ladder. It shows that the rim operator’s extremal eigenvalue diverges at the flux value where the edge charge jumps, providing a numerical check on this charge transfer mechanism.

papers.title: Local field shifts and the Gribov-Zwanziger horizon functional
papers.abstract: We study a Maggiore-Schaden-like re-centering of the Gribov-Zwanziger action using a smooth compactly supported profile. At fixed background and finite cutoff, under the stated coercivity and contour hypotheses, this transformation preserves the original horizon functional with no residual dependence on the profile. The extension to gauge-field integration requires additional domination assumptions. Near a self-adjoint first Gribov horizon, the response depends on both the lowest Faddeev-Popov eigenvalue and its source weight. We extend this visibility analysis to non-self-adjoint compressions, separating source darkness from truncation-induced shielding, and recall continuum transverse $SU(2)$ examples. Transporting the composite insertion preserves the regulated Gaussian and resolvent structure. A separate free-space tree-level check reproduces the auxiliary-mass denominator of the RGZ propagator, without determining condensate dynamics
papers.summary: This paper investigates a smooth, compactly supported re‑centering of the Gribov–Zwanziger action, showing that the horizon functional remains unchanged under certain coercivity and contour conditions. It also explores the dependence of the response near the first Gribov horizon on the lowest Faddeev–Popov eigenvalue and provides a tree‑level check reproducing the RGZ propagator denominator.

papers.title: Renormalization Group Flow from 4d Chern-Simons Theory
papers.abstract: The four-dimensional Chern-Simons theory coupled with surface defects is known to realize two-dimensional integrable quantum field theories (QFTs). We discuss the renormalization group (RG) flow of such two-dimensional integrable QFTs from first-principles Feynman diagram computations intrinsically in the four-dimensional framework. We first derive the one-loop RG flow of two-dimensional QFTs realized by the four-dimensional Chern-Simons theory on $\Sigma \times C$ coupled with the order surface defects supported on $\Sigma $. Here, the affine Kac-Moody symmetry of the defects underlies the one-loop RG flow. We then derive the one-loop RG flow of the principal chiral model (PCM) without Wess-Zumino term, which is realized using disorder surface defects, within the Batalin-Vilkovisky formalism. We obtain the nontrivial one-loop RG flow of the PCM, reproducing its known asymptotically-free beta function, using two complementary methods: by explicitly evaluating one-loop Feynman amplitudes, and by computing an analogue of analytic torsion for four-dimensional Chern-Simons theory.
papers.summary: This work derives the one-loop renormalization group flow for two-dimensional integrable quantum field theories realized via four-dimensional Chern‑Simons theory with surface defects, using both explicit Feynman diagram calculations and an analytic torsion analogue. In particular, it reproduces the asymptotically free beta function of the principal chiral model without a Wess–Zumino term, illustrating how four-dimensional gauge dynamics encode two-dimensional integrable dynamics.

papers.title: Confinement--Higgs Complementarity Viewed through Relative Quantum Reference Frames
papers.abstract: We formulate confinement--Higgs complementarity in terms of the relative orientation between two independently constructed quantum reference frames (QRFs): one derived from the gauge field and the other from the scalar field. Exact continuum and lattice identities give a relational interpretation of the scalar--color observables used in recent gauge-fixing-free $SU(2)$ simulations. In particular, we provide a QRF interpretation of the additional gauge-invariant nonlocal separation line obtained from the Cho--Duan--Ge (CDG) reduction reported in lattice simulations of the radially fixed fundamental $SU(2)$ gauge--scalar model. We explain why such a candidate nonlocal boundary is compatible with Fradkin--Shenker continuity and Osterwalder--Seiler analyticity for the appropriate class of local gauge-invariant observables. Separately, we show that a Wilson-rooted control observable admits an exact results at zero plaquette coupling and that it does not cause such a nonlocal separation line.
papers.summary: The paper reformulates confinement–Higgs complementarity using relative quantum reference frames built from gauge and scalar fields, providing a relational interpretation of gauge-invariant observables in SU(2) gauge–scalar lattice simulations. It shows that a nonlocal separation line from Cho–Duan–Ge reduction is compatible with Fradkin–Shenker continuity and that a Wilson-rooted observable does not induce such a line.

papers.title: A proof of Nakamura's conjecture
papers.abstract: We prove Nakamura's conjecture on the relation between the 2D Toda model and solutions of the Ernst equation, using the Pfaffian solutions obtained in our previous work arXiv:2610.27420.
papers.summary: This paper establishes a rigorous proof of Nakamura's conjecture linking the 2D Toda integrable hierarchy to solutions of the Ernst equation in general relativity, employing Pfaffian techniques developed in their earlier work. The result clarifies the algebraic structure underlying the integrable reduction of Einstein's equations, but does not directly address the physicist's listed interests such as holography or conformal blocks.

papers.title: Negative and Positive Saddle-Selection Ambiguities in the HTEE
papers.authors: H. Ebrahim, M. Ali-Akbari, K. Taheranvarian
papers.abstract: The holographic timelike entanglement entropy (HTEE), computed via complexified extremal surfaces, suffers from a saddle-selection ambiguity: for sufficiently small time intervals (\(\Delta t\to0\)), both a vacuum-connected and a vacuum-disconnected complex extremal surface contribute, and the minimal-real-part criterion and the vacuum-reduction criterion can favor different saddles. We study this ambiguity in strongly coupled field theories whose dual geometries are hyperscaling-violating Lifshitz backgrounds, in which conformal symmetry and Lorentz invariance are broken by the Lifshitz exponent and the hyperscaling-violation parameter. Working in \(2+1\)- and \(3+1\)-dimensional dual field theories, we derive general expressions for the HTEE in the vacuum-connected and vacuum-disconnected saddles, \(s_{v.c.}\) and \(s_{v.d.}\), respectively, and compare their real parts. We find that the two criteria agree everywhere except at the first accidental zero. The ambiguity appears in two distinct forms. In the \emph{negative} family, \(\operatorname{Re}(s_{v.c.})=0\) and \(\operatorname{Re}(s_{v.d.})<0\), whereas in the \emph{positive} family, \(\operatorname{Re}(s_{v.c.})>0\) and \(\operatorname{Re}(s_{v.d.})=0\). The latter shows that the ambiguity survives even in the conformal \(3+1\)-dimensional case. It therefore seems that the saddle-selection ambiguity is a generic feature of the complexified-geometry prescription.
papers.summary: The paper analyzes the saddle‑selection ambiguity that arises when computing holographic timelike entanglement entropy via complexified extremal surfaces in hyperscaling‑violating Lifshitz geometries. It shows that both vacuum‑connected and vacuum‑disconnected saddles can dominate depending on the time interval, a phenomenon that persists even in conformal 3+1‑dimensional theories, indicating a generic feature of the complexified‑geometry prescription.

papers.title: Entanglement and Charge Transfer
papers.abstract: We compute the entropic order parameter introduced in (1905.10487) using the replica trick for two disjoint intervals. For a global symmetry, this quantity measures the mutual information carried by charge-anticharge intertwiners. We formulate the problem in terms of averages over twisted partition functions on replica Riemann surfaces, and obtain exact solutions for free fermions and compact bosons, for $U(1)$ symmetry and its discrete $\mathbb Z_N$ subgroups. We show that further averaging over both families of non-contractible cycles gives access to an additional quantity, which is the loss of Holevo information associated with complementary-charge measurements that occurs upon removing the intertwiners. For the boson, this quantity vanishes, whereas for Dirac fermions it equals the difference between the mutual information of the fermion-parity-gauged and ungauged theories, independently of the choice of even $\mathbb Z_N$ subgroup. Finally, we extend the analysis to non-Abelian symmetries using saddle expansions, deriving universal behavior in the nearly touching intervals limit and for a large number of fermions $N_F\gg1$.
papers.summary: The paper computes an entropic order parameter for disjoint intervals using the replica trick, deriving exact results for free fermions and compact bosons with U(1) and Z_N symmetries, and explores the associated Holevo information loss. It extends the analysis to non‑Abelian symmetries via saddle expansions, revealing universal behavior in the nearly touching limit and for large numbers of fermions.

papers.title: Algebraic instantons and non-Gaussian vacuum in quantum mechanics
papers.authors: Rahim Aziz, Hao Geng, Thomas Schaefer, Mithat \"Unsal
papers.abstract: The standard instanton calculus in quantum mechanics is based on harmonic minima in the potential. When the perturbative vacuum is anharmonic, $V\simeq\lambda x^{2n}$ with $n\ge2$, the standard construction fails. We study this problem for a particle on a circle and subject to a potential $V(x)=16\lambda\sin^4(x/2)$. The instanton and its fluctuation operator are known in closed form, but they differ qualitatively from the familiar ones. Because $V''=0$ at the minimum, the classical vacuum is gapless, the instanton decays algebraically (an algebraic instanton), the zero mode is located at the threshold of a continuous spectrum, and the one-loop determinant is infrared divergent. Quantum mechanics generates a non-perturbative gap $E_q\propto\hbar^{4/3}\lambda^{1/3}$, and the instanton is embedded in a vacuum that is dynamically gapped, similar to what happens in Yang--Mills theory. We show that the one-instanton amplitude can be computed by matching the instanton trajectory to the exact vacuum part of the path integral. The resulting prefactor scales as $\hbar^{4/3}$, and this expression agrees with the numerical spectrum to a very high accuracy. The classical interaction between instantons decays as $T^{-3}$, whereas the correct result is an exponential decay controlled by the dynamically generated gap, beyond the quantum time scale. We provide an alternative derivation of this result based on a sum over intermediate states.
papers.summary: The authors analyze instanton solutions in a quantum mechanical system with an anharmonic potential V=16λsin^4(x/2), finding that the instanton is algebraic, the one‑loop determinant diverges, and a non‑perturbative gap E_q∝ħ^{4/3}λ^{1/3} is dynamically generated. They compute the one‑instanton amplitude by matching the instanton trajectory to the exact vacuum part of the path integral, obtaining a prefactor scaling as ħ^{4/3} that agrees with numerical spectra.

papers.title: Wilsonian renormalization group flow in QED with the Pauli term
papers.abstract:
We study the renormalization group (RG) flow of quantum electrodynamics (QED) with a Pauli term, $\kappa_	au\Bar{\psi}\sigma_{\mu
u}F_{\mu
u}\psi$, by using the gradient flow exact renormalization group (GFERG). In the GFERG, the gauge Ward--Takahashi identity takes the conventional form and is exactly preserved, and the gauge coupling flows only through the photon anomalous dimension~$\gamma_A$. In the leading large-$N_f$ approximation, the vacuum polarization induced by the Pauli coupling yields a nontrivial fixed point with~$e_*=0$, $\kappa_*
eq0$, and~$\gamma_A=-1$. This fixed point has three relevant directions, as does one of the fixed points of the asymptotically safe QED proposed by Gies and Ziebell. At finite~$N_f$, however, the $N_f$-independent one-loop effects on the fermion line, in particular the additive mass renormalization proportional to~$\kappa^2$, eliminate this fixed point unless $N_f$ is at least several tens; for~$N_f=1$ there is no fixed point at weak Pauli coupling. Along the full flow for~$N_f=1$, $\kappa_	au$ is irrelevant and is attracted to an induced value~$\kappa_{	ext{ind}}(e_	au)$, which is proportional to~$e_	au^3$ at weak coupling, while $e_	au^2$ is marginally irrelevant as in QED without the Pauli term.
papers.summary: This paper analyzes the RG flow of QED augmented by a Pauli interaction using the gradient flow exact RG, uncovering a nontrivial fixed point in the large‑N_f limit with vanishing gauge coupling but nonzero Pauli coupling. At finite N_f the fixed point disappears unless N_f is large, and for N_f=1 the Pauli term is irrelevant, flowing to a value proportional to e^3 while the gauge coupling remains marginally irrelevant.

papers.title: On $\iota$Quiver (BPS) Algebras and (Strict) Partitions
papers.abstract: We consider the $\iota$quiver algebras of split type associated with the quiver BPS algebras of affine type A. They are supposed to give twisted affine Yangians and (elliptic) $\iota$quantum toroidal algebras that could possibly arise from D-branes on $\mathbb{C}\times\mathbb{C}^2/\mathbb{Z}_n$ with orientifolds. We mention some properties of these algebras, such as the minimalistic presentations in the rational cases and the coideal structures. We also investigate how one might identify these algebras from the quiver theories with orientifold actions. Moreover, we discuss some representations with combinatorial bases of these algebras. In particular, the algebras with $n=1,2$ in certain limits of the parameters have representations labelled by (coloured) strict/symmetric partitions, which in the case of $n=1$ recovers the known BPS counting of certain theories.
papers.summary: The paper studies iotaQuiver algebras of split type associated with affine type A quiver BPS algebras, proposing they realize twisted affine Yangians and elliptic iota quantum toroidal algebras that could arise from D-branes on $mathbb{C}	imesmathbb{C}^2/mathbb{Z}_n$ with orientifolds. It also explores minimal presentations, coideal structures, and combinatorial representations labeled by strict/symmetric partitions, connecting to BPS counting in certain limits.

papers.title: Towards a foundation model for Type IIB flux vacua
papers.authors: Sven Krippendorf, Magdalena Larfors, Zhimei Liu, Andreas Schachner, Moritz Walden
papers.abstract: Progress in characterising the Type IIB flux landscape requires scalable methods for constructing flux vacua. In this work, we investigate generative models as a framework for sampling vacua across multiple Calabi-Yau geometries and for directing searches towards specified physical properties. We compare transformers and diffusion models trained to generate quantised fluxes together with approximate values of the complex structure moduli and axio-dilaton. We exploit a staged training procedure comprising pre-training, and post-training via reinforcement learning, and assess how each stage improves the generated distributions and enables targeted sampling. We further examine whether structures learned from geometries with smaller $h^{1,2}$ can be transferred to geometries with larger $h^{1,2}$ through fine-tuning on specialised datasets. Our results provide evidence that generative models can learn distributions of flux vacua across distinct compactifications, improve searches for vacua with selected properties and transfer information between geometries. This establishes a concrete basis for developing a foundation model of the Type IIB flux landscape.
papers.summary: This paper explores transformer and diffusion generative models to efficiently sample Type IIB flux vacua across various Calabi‑Yau geometries, using staged pre‑training and reinforcement learning to target specific physical properties. It demonstrates that such models can transfer learned distributions between compactifications and guide searches for vacua with desired characteristics, laying groundwork for a universal flux‑landscape foundation model.

papers.title: Neumann zero modes and the locality of the derivative expansion
papers.authors: C. D. Fosco, F. D. Mazzitelli
papers.abstract: The derivative expansion (DE) provides a useful approximation to the Casimir interaction energy between two close surfaces. It has the form of a local functional, obtained from a zero momentum expansion. However, when the system involves a massless field satisfying Neumann conditions, that expansion may develop nonanalytic terms. We present here a study on how this property reflects itself in the need to add to the DE some novel, nonlocal terms. These are, we argue, akin to the ones introduced in effective theories because of the presence of massless particles in loops. We pinpoint the mode responsible for this effect, and construct the effective action due to its fluctuations, showing that it reproduces known nonanalytic contributions, and present the corresponding nonlocal addition to the DE. We also predict a new nonanalyticity: Neumann conditions in $3+1$ dimensions at zero temperature produce a term of order $|{\mathbf k}_\shortparallel |^3$, with a parameter-free coefficient, between the (local) second and fourth orders of the expansion. We show that, for a cylinder in front of a plane, the zero-mode loop adds to the local expansion a term of relative order $(L/R)^{3/2}$, with a coefficient that we compute explicitly, showing that it accounts for the behaviour of the existing numerical fits for that geometry.
papers.summary: The paper analyzes how Neumann boundary conditions for a massless field introduce nonanalytic terms in the derivative expansion of Casimir energies, requiring nonlocal corrections to the local functional. It predicts a new |k|³ term in 3+1 dimensions and quantifies its impact on the cylinder‑plane geometry, matching numerical data.

papers.title: On reflection positivity of lattice chiral fermions
papers.abstract: We point out that the overlap Weyl fermion, the spacetime lattice realization of a Weyl fermion underlying L\"uscher's construction of lattice chiral gauge theories, is not reflection positive in two and four dimensions at finite lattice spacing. Consequently, the standard Osterwalder--Schrader reconstruction does not yield a Hilbert space with a self-adjoint Hamiltonian. In two dimensions, we further show that the overlap Weyl fermion cannot be cut open: the lattice action becomes nonlocal in the presence of a boundary, as expected from the gravitational anomaly of the continuum field theory. By contrast, the overlap Dirac fermion is known to be reflection positive. However, its compact axial symmetry is not invariant under the reflection, whereas a reflection-invariant axial symmetry is noncompact, and both are part of an Onsager algebra.
papers.summary: The paper shows that the overlap Weyl fermion on a lattice fails reflection positivity in 2 and 4 dimensions, preventing a standard Osterwalder–Schrader reconstruction of a self‑adjoint Hamiltonian. It further demonstrates that the lattice action becomes non‑local when a boundary is introduced, reflecting the gravitational anomaly of the continuum theory.

papers.title: Equivariant Localization with Electric Monodromy in M-theory
papers.abstract: We extend equivariant localization for supersymmetric AdS$_3$ backgrounds of M-theory to solutions with nonzero electric flux periods. The associated local electric potential acquires additive monodromy, contributing to the warped volume alongside R-symmetry fixed points and outer boundaries. Using Killing-spinor identities, we relate the electric periods to magnetic flux and, for a class of compact backgrounds, the warped volume to the electric Maxwell charge. We also derive a relation between the gravitational anomaly and the electric flux. We apply these results to AdS$_3$ $\times S^3 \times S^3 \times T^2$ and AdS$_3$ $\times S^3 \times K3 \times S^1$, recovering their central charges and deriving the R-current levels of the former directly from eleven-dimensional supergravity. Finally, we study a noncompact half-BPS AdS$_3$ $\times S^3\times S^3$ geometry fibered over a periodic half-cylinder, where fixed-point, monodromy and outer-boundary contributions coexist.
papers.summary: The authors extend equivariant localization to M‑theory AdS$_3$ backgrounds with nonzero electric flux periods, deriving explicit relations between electric periods, magnetic flux, and the warped volume that allow the computation of central charges and R‑current levels for compact geometries such as AdS$_3	imes S^3	imes S^3	imes T^2$ and AdS$_3	imes S^3	imes K3	imes S^1$. They further analyze a noncompact half‑BPS AdS$_3	imes S^3	imes S^3$ geometry fibered over a periodic half‑cylinder, demonstrating how fixed‑point, monodromy, and outer‑boundary contributions coexist in the localization formula.

papers.title: On Thermodynamics of AdS Black Holes in Square-Root Nonlinear Electrodynamics
papers.authors: A. Belhaj, S. E. Ennadifi, M. Jemri, M. Nach
papers.abstract: Inspired by exponential Maxwell models, we propose a new black hole solution in square root nonlinear electrodynamics. Using the analogy between black hole mechanics and thermodynamics, we investigate the corresponding stability, the P-v criticality and the phase transitions. As a result, we find that the obtained black hole exhibits Van der Waals behaviors without additional corrections which typically appear in universal ratio computations.
papers.summary: The authors construct a new AdS black hole solution in a square‑root nonlinear electrodynamics model and analyze its thermodynamic behavior, finding Van der Waals–like phase transitions without extra corrections. This work extends the study of black hole thermodynamics in modified electrodynamics, offering potential insights for holographic duals.

papers.title: Decoding SO(5) Deconfined Multicriticality: Conformal Bootstrap and Fuzzy-Sphere Spectroscopy
papers.abstract: The nature of the deconfined quantum critical point (DQCP) remains unsettled: competing explanations invoke a real multicritical conformal field theory (CFT) or pseudocriticality governed by nearby complex fixed points. We use the conformal bootstrap and fuzzy-sphere regularization to compute $SO(5)$ CFT data and compare our results with large-scale quantum Monte Carlo (QMC) data to investigate these scenarios. Using mixed correlators of the lowest vector $\phi$, singlet $s$, and traceless symmetric scalar $t$, we characterize the bootstrap cone whose tip lies remarkably close to the position indicated by large-scale QMC. We extract an extensive spectrum across $SO(5)$ irreducible representations, together with operator product expansion (OPE) coefficients. We study a fuzzy-sphere realization of the $SO(5)$ nonlinear sigma model with a level-1 Wess--Zumino--Witten term. Using the special conformal generators, we identify 52 conformal primaries in a system with \(N=10\) Landau orbitals, including 31 not previously classified as primaries in the earlier fuzzy-sphere study. Symmetry projection extends fuzzy-sphere exact diagonalization to $N=12$. The bootstrap spectrum and OPE coefficients show close agreement with fuzzy-sphere data, including 16 of the newly identified primaries in channels accessible to the mixed-correlator bootstrap. The lowest $SO(5)$ singlet scalar is relevant in the bootstrap and QMC results; its fuzzy-sphere data is $\Delta_s=2.816$ at $N=12$ and decreases with system size. Our results suggest that the mixed-correlator bootstrap solution represents a unitary CFT with a relevant $SO(5)$ singlet scalar and is closely connected to the QMC and fuzzy-sphere data for the DQCP. The conformal bootstrap, fuzzy-sphere, and QMC together provide comprehensive evidence for an $SO(5)$ multicritical CFT and critical data to decode the phases in two-dimensional quantum magnets.
papers.summary: This work applies the mixed‑correlator conformal bootstrap to the SO(5) symmetric deconfined quantum critical point, extracting a detailed spectrum and OPE data that agree with both fuzzy‑sphere lattice regularization and large‑scale QMC simulations. The results support the existence of a unitary SO(5) multicritical CFT with a relevant singlet scalar, offering a concrete benchmark for future studies of two‑dimensional quantum magnets.

papers.title: Off-shell one-loop counterterms of Palatini gravity with an independent background connection
papers.authors: F. T. Brandt, G. A. Menezes
papers.abstract: We compute the one-loop divergences of pure gravity in the first-order (Palatini) formulation, using the background field method in Goldberg variables, with a background connection independent of the background metric. Background Ward-Takahashi identities are verified at one loop. The divergences of the two-point functions, obtained in arbitrary dimension and gauge, require, besides the curvature-squared terms, invariants built from the nonmetricity of the background connection; in particular, the Gauss-Bonnet combination, which is not topological for a nonmetric connection, does not suffice. Three- and four-point functions in the Feynman-de Donder gauge complete the counterterm Lagrangian up to fourth order in the nonmetricity and provide parameter-free tests of it. All the counterterms vanish on shell, as in the metric formulation, and off shell they can be removed by field redefinitions.
papers.summary: The paper evaluates one-loop divergences in Palatini gravity using a background field method with an independent background connection, finding that the counterterms involve curvature-squared terms and additional invariants built from nonmetricity beyond the Gauss‑Bonnet combination. All divergences vanish on shell and can be removed by field redefinitions, confirming consistency with the metric formulation.

papers.title: Phase Structure and Thermodynamic Geometry of STU Black Holes
papers.authors: Fil Simovic, Kenan Scavennec, David Kubiznak, Robert B. Mann
papers.abstract: We study the thermodynamics of four-dimensional STU black holes, a family of charged solutions of gauged N = 8, SO(8) supergravity, from the perspective of geometric thermodynamics. We focus on non-rotating solutions carrying pairwise-equal charges, obtaining closed-form expressions for the thermodynamic quantities directly in terms of the physical charges, and use them to determine the equation of state and associated phase structure. We also construct the Ruppeiner geometry for the STU black hole, taking the temperature and thermodynamic volume as fluctuation variables, and study its renormalized curvature as a probe of the black hole microstructure. We find a rich phase structure with two critical points present whenever the charge ratio is sufficiently large, and identify regions in parameter space associated with attractive and repulsive microscopic interactions.
papers.summary: The paper presents a detailed thermodynamic analysis of non-rotating STU black holes in four-dimensional gauged N=8 supergravity, deriving closed-form expressions for entropy, temperature, and equation of state in terms of physical charges. It further explores the Ruppeiner geometry, revealing a rich phase structure with two critical points and insights into microscopic interactions.

papers.title: Triple Exchange at the Cosmological Collider in Closed Form
papers.authors: Taushif Ahmed, Sumit Banik, Syed Mehedi Hasan, Andreas Rapakoulias
papers.abstract: Particles with masses near the Hubble scale leave a characteristic pattern in the primordial bispectrum, turning inflation into a cosmological collider. For light fields, where this signal is largest, no closed form is known for the full shape of the quasi-single-field triple exchange. Using Feynman-integral methods, we obtain the first closed-form results, exact in the momenta, as expansions in terms of multiple polylogarithms around the massless and conformally coupled limits. We show that the template used in Planck analyses overestimates the amplitude by up to a factor of 1.8 and underestimates the mass, whereas our new template recovers both, as needed for current and upcoming CMB and galaxy surveys. We also compute the collapsed trispectrum and, combining it with the bispectrum, find that at weak mixing it bounds the self-coupling more tightly.
papers.summary: The authors derive the first closed-form expression for the quasi-single-field triple-exchange bispectrum, expanding it in multiple polylogarithms around massless and conformally coupled limits, and show that Planck templates overestimate the signal. They also compute the collapsed trispectrum, tightening bounds on the self-coupling at weak mixing, providing new templates for upcoming CMB and galaxy surveys.

papers.title: Holographic Homogeneous Black Branes from Anisotropic Scaling
papers.abstract: We construct homogeneous anisotropic black branes in Einstein gravity and Einstein--Maxwell--dilaton theory in arbitrary spacetime dimensions. By imposing compatibility between radial scaling and the spatial Lie algebra, we reduce the field equations to radial equations and algebraic constraints on the scaling exponents, curvature, and matter fields. We construct neutral, electric, magnetic, and dyonic solutions, including explicit five-dimensional Bianchi geometries and higher-dimensional families supported by Ricci nilsolitons. We investigate the thermodynamics of these solutions, obtaining their Euclidean action, mass, and entropy scaling. We also study the dynamics of a massive probe scalar, deriving an asymptotic mass bound and an exact purely damped quasinormal spectrum for a particular class of scaling geometries. Numerical calculations further explore the mass, dynamical exponent, and momentum dependence of scalar relaxation in Nil, Solv, and Bianchi type VI geometries. Our results establish a framework for studying thermodynamic and dynamical properties of homogeneous anisotropic scaling geometries that are generally not asymptotically locally anti-de Sitter.
papers.summary: We construct homogeneous anisotropic black branes in Einstein and Einstein-Maxwell-dilaton theories, deriving radial equations and algebraic constraints that yield neutral, electric, magnetic, and dyonic solutions in arbitrary dimensions. The work also analyzes their thermodynamics and scalar probe dynamics, providing exact quasinormal spectra and numerical studies of relaxation in Nil, Solv, and Bianchi type VI geometries.

papers.title: Doubly-spinning Black Saturns
papers.abstract: We construct a six-parameter family of stationary, asymptotically flat solutions of five-dimensional vacuum Einstein gravity describing a spherical black hole surrounded by a black ring, with rotation in both independent planes. In a specific regime both horizons can become extremal, thereby providing the first example of a regular asymptotically flat vacuum Einstein solution with two extremal disconnected horizons. We also show that while non-extremal black Saturns can be in thermodynamic equilibrium, the doubly extremal Saturn cannot. The solution admits the doubly spinning Myers-Perry, the Pomeransky-Sen'kov black ring, and the singly spinning black Saturn as regular limits. We also show agreement with earlier blackfold predictions for the phase diagram of these solutions.
papers.summary: This paper presents a six-parameter family of five‑dimensional vacuum solutions describing a spherical black hole surrounded by a rotating black ring, allowing both horizons to become extremal. It also discusses thermodynamic equilibrium and connects to earlier blackfold predictions.

papers.title: A note on Padmanabhan's path-integral duality
papers.authors: P. Fernandez de Cordoba, J. M. Isidro
papers.abstract: We develop a field-theoretic implementation of Padmanabhan's principle of invariance under the duality $\mathcal S \rightarrow {L_0^2}/{\mathcal S}$, where ${\mathcal S}$ is the proper length (the action integral along a particle's trajectory) and $L_0$ is a quantum of length. Starting from the particle propagator and its Schwinger proper-time representation, we derive the wave operator associated with the duality transformation in terms of a scalar field, rather than a point particle. The resulting theory is governed by a nonlocal operator involving modified Bessel functions. We analyse the infrared and ultraviolet regimes, demonstrate the recovery of standard Klein-Gordon theory at low energies, and show the appearance of exponential ultraviolet suppression. Our analysis provides a natural extension, to quantum field theory, of Padmanabhan's duality for point particles.
papers.summary: This paper extends Padmanabhan's path-integral duality to quantum field theory by deriving a nonlocal wave operator built from modified Bessel functions, which reproduces the Klein–Gordon equation in the infrared and yields exponential UV suppression. The analysis shows how the duality acts on the proper-time representation of the particle propagator and provides a field-theoretic framework for length quantization.

papers.title: Quantum chaos from time-dependent CFT states at large central charge
papers.authors: Shaun D. Hampton, Pantelis Panopoulos, Gideon Vos
papers.abstract: We provide a first study of the behavior of four probes on heavy, time-dependent background states of conformal field theories at large central charge. Employing the monodromy method and including subleading corrections to the identity block, we compute the correlation function of two light and two middle-heavy operators on such a heavy background, by switching on a small interaction between the light and middle-heavy sectors. Summing the discontinuity contributions and analytically continuing from Euclidean to Lorentzian signature, we show that the out-of-time-ordered correlator (OTOC) exhibits maximal chaos, that is, the Lyapunov exponent saturates the MSS bound.
papers.summary: The paper studies four-point functions of light and middle-heavy operators in heavy, time-dependent CFT backgrounds at large central charge, using the monodromy method to include subleading corrections to the identity block. It finds that the resulting out-of-time-ordered correlator saturates the MSS chaos bound, indicating maximal chaos in these states.

papers.title: From Quasinormal Mode Poles to Branch Cuts at Finite $N$
papers.abstract: In the strict large-$N$ limit, holographic thermal retarded correlators are typigcally meromorphic, with their late-time behavior determined by isolated quasinormal mode (QNM) poles. We show that the first bulk-loop correction, of order $1/N^2$, qualitatively changes this structure. In a scalar theory on the planar AdS$_5$ black brane, a one-loop bulk diagram generates poles at sums of two QNM frequencies at fixed loop momentum $q$; integration over the continuous momentum turns these QNM-pair poles into branch cuts. At vanishing external spatial momentum, for pairs built from QNM branches with opposite real parts, the leading light-cone contributions cancel at large momentum, and the residual QNM-pair frequency scales as $q^{-1/3}$. Consequently, an infinite family of cuts accumulates at zero frequency, while all tree-level QNM poles remain at finite nonzero frequencies. The first finite-$N$ correction therefore closes the gap set by the classical QNM spectrum. Competition between the decreasing QNM-pair damping and thermal Boltzmann suppression produces a moving saddle and a finite-$N$ contribution $G(t)\sim N^{-2}t^\alpha e^{-Ct^{3/4}},\, C>0,$ which decays more slowly than the leading classical QNM contribution. Thus the large-$N$ expansion is nonuniform at late times, and bulk quantum fluctuations generate a distinct late-time regime beyond the classical QNM decay.
papers.summary: The paper shows that at order 1/N^2 bulk-loop corrections in AdS5 black brane turn isolated QNM poles into branch cuts, producing an infinite family of cuts accumulating at zero frequency and altering late-time decay. This demonstrates a nonuniform large-N expansion and a new late-time regime beyond classical QNM decay.

papers.title: Higher-point amplitudes and recursion relations from the worldsheet in complex Liouville string
papers.abstract: We consider multipoint perturbative string amplitudes in genus zero in complex Liouville string theory (CLS) in the worldsheet approach. Based on explicit worldsheet calculations and analytic bootstrap, we first compute correlators involving ground ring operators, which additionally depend on a choice of integration cycle on the moduli space. Using this result and higher equations of motion in Liouville theory, we calculate higher-point tachyon correlators with one degenerate field and explain what contributions were missed in previous attempts to apply this method in the literature. This allows us to derive a recursion formula, which agrees with the general recursion for amplitudes known from "matrix model" approach to CLS. We also propose an expression for correlators with ground ring insertions in terms of tautological classes on the moduli space of curves and comment on generalization of these results to the case of rational minimal strings.
papers.summary: The paper derives a recursion formula for genus‑zero complex Liouville string amplitudes by computing ground‑ring and tachyon correlators on the worldsheet, matching the matrix‑model result. It also proposes a geometric expression for ground‑ring insertions in terms of tautological classes, extending to rational minimal strings.

papers.title: Thermal deep inelastic scattering, universality and complex geodesics
papers.abstract: In deep inelastic scattering (DIS), a lepton scatters off a target hadron whose structure is probed by an exchanged photon with large spacelike virtuality. We consider two-point functions of currents in strongly interacting quantum field theories at finite temperature in this kinematic regime and use a holographic description to compute them. At large virtuality, the crossover from vacuum-dominated to thermally dominated physics corresponds to a transition from exponentially suppressed absorption to power-law behavior of the response functions. This regime is related to a particular near-lightcone limit of thermal CFT correlators. We show that the response functions exhibit a large degree of universality: the dependence on the three-point couplings of currents to the stress tensor enters through a channel-dependent coefficient multiplying the kinematic parameter that controls the relative size of vacuum and thermal effects. The same coefficient controls conformal collider bounds; when either bound is saturated, the corresponding response function takes its vacuum form in the near-lightcone limit. Furthermore, the absorption exponent in the low-temperature regime is related to a complex geodesic propagating in the near-lightcone geometry.
papers.summary: The paper studies deep inelastic scattering in strongly coupled finite-temperature QFTs using holography, showing a transition from vacuum-dominated to thermal behavior in the response functions. It finds universal behavior governed by a channel-dependent coefficient linked to conformal collider bounds and relates the absorption exponent to complex geodesics in the near-lightcone geometry.

papers.title: Soft momentum expansion about the Stokes topological limit of Bogoliubov coefficients
papers.authors: Daniel J. H. Chung, Nidhi Sudhir, Junqi Zhang
papers.abstract: It is known that particle production in time-dependent cosmological backgrounds can be computed using the Stokes phenomena occurring in Bogoliubov transformations with an analytically continued time coordinate. We analytically compute the soft momentum expansion of the particle production amplitude about the Stokes topological limit that was recently discovered in this context. The computational technique relies on an exponentially improved asymptotic expansion that involves automorphisms in the space of functions defined partly by the angular step function intrinsic to the Stokes topological sectors. We combine this with special discrete symmetries tied to the time dependence of the dispersion relation $\omega_k^2(z) = C(k) + A z^n$ for even $n$ to explicitly compute the leading momentum dependence of the amplitude which is nonperturbative in $A$. We also use this result to give a semi-analytic estimate of the number density of particles in this class of scenarios.
papers.summary: The paper derives the soft momentum expansion of particle production amplitudes in time-dependent cosmological backgrounds by exploiting Stokes phenomena in Bogoliubov transformations. It uses an exponentially improved asymptotic expansion and discrete symmetries of the dispersion relation to obtain nonperturbative leading momentum dependence and a semi-analytic estimate of particle number density.

papers.title: Lifting asymptotic symmetries from metric to tetrad formulation
papers.abstract: Metric solution spaces defined by gauge and boundary conditions are associated with a residual symmetry algebra, consisting of the diffeomorphism generators whose action preserves these conditions. Describing a metric solution space in terms of tetrad variables adds a local Lorentz freedom. When part of this freedom is fixed by additional tetrad gauge and boundary conditions, metric residual symmetries must be supplemented by compensating Lorentz transformations. If a residual Lorentz freedom remains, there is an ambiguity in these compensating transformations. The most direct choices generally fail to realize the metric residual symmetry algebra as a subalgebra of the tetrad one, because of a field-dependent cocycle. We show that a reference tetrad, that is a section of the tetrad solution space seen as a principal bundle over the metric one, always provides a lift free of this cocycle, so that the tetrad residual symmetry algebra is the semi-direct sum of the metric one and the ideal of field-dependent residual Lorentz transformations. The construction is independent of the gauge conditions, of the residual group, of the first-order Lagrangian, and reduces to the Kosmann lift on metric isometry generators. We illustrate it on a Weyl BMS-type solution space with time-dependent boundary metric, described in tetrad variables with a residual U(1) Lorentz freedom, for which the cocycle of a naive lift is computed and then explicitly removed.
papers.summary: The paper develops a systematic method to lift residual diffeomorphism symmetries of metric solution spaces to the tetrad formalism, resolving field‑dependent cocycles by introducing a reference tetrad. This construction clarifies how the tetrad residual symmetry algebra decomposes into the metric algebra plus field‑dependent Lorentz transformations, with explicit application to a Weyl‑BMS type space relevant for time‑dependent boundary metrics.

papers.title: Carroll Double Copy
papers.authors: Sucheta Majumdar, Silvia Nagy, Giorgio Pizzolo
papers.abstract: We construct a double copy for Carroll gravity as the ``square'' of Carroll Yang-Mills theory at the linearised level. Starting from the convolutional double copy prescription in Lorentzian spacetime, we take the Carrollian limit $c \rightarrow 0$ to establish a double copy dictionary compatible both with symmetries and the corresponding equations of motion. Since this limit yields two distinct sectors, namely the electric and magnetic Carroll theories, we systematically investigate double copy constructions involving all possible combinations of these parent theories. To accommodate the time-independent on-shell configurations of the magnetic Carroll fields, we introduce a suitable regularisation procedure for the convolutional double copy. In addition, the covariance of the double copy under Carroll boosts requires an appropriate dressing of the fields, leading to the inclusion of a Goldstone-type object in the construction. We first develop the formalism using toy models involving scalar fields and then apply it to the double copy between linearised Carroll Yang-Mills theory and Carroll gravity.
papers.summary: This paper develops a linearised double copy between Carrollian Yang-Mills and Carroll gravity, extending the convolutional double copy to the ultra‑relativistic limit. It introduces a regularisation for time‑independent magnetic fields and a Goldstone dressing to preserve Carroll boost covariance.

papers.title: Instant Folded Strings: Fractal Decay and ANEC Saturation
papers.abstract: Instant Folded Strings (IFSs) present a puzzle. On the one hand, they appear to be an intrinsic part of string theory: they are fundamental closed strings nucleated classically in backgrounds in which the string coupling grows toward the future, and they have been argued to play an important role in black-hole interiors and cosmology. On the other hand, their energy-momentum tensor violates the Averaged Null Energy Condition (ANEC), placing IFSs in tension with standard causality and unitarity arguments. We show that finite string coupling resolves this tension by triggering a decay cascade that saturates the ANEC in Minkowski spacetime. The remnant of the original IFS persists indefinitely, continuously seeding a self-similar fragmentation cascade that produces infinitely many strings over its full history. In the semiclassical regime, the cascade is governed by a single Malthusian exponent, $\kappa_{\mathrm{IFS}}=2\sqrt{2}-2$, which controls the branching growth, pressure decay, cutoff-ANEC convergence, and anomalous non-integer dependence on the string coupling. The complete state has vanishing total energy and momentum while remaining highly excited and carrying negative integrated pressure on every finite time slice. This provides a concrete example of genuinely stringy low-energy dynamics in which microscopic null-energy consistency coexists with macroscopic negative pressure.
papers.summary: The paper investigates instant folded strings that nucleate in backgrounds with growing string coupling and initially violate the Averaged Null Energy Condition, but demonstrates that finite coupling induces a self-similar decay cascade that saturates the ANEC while leaving a zero-energy remnant. The cascade is governed by a Malthusian exponent κ=2√2−2, producing fractal fragmentation and negative pressure on every finite time slice, thereby providing a concrete example of stringy dynamics that reconcile microscopic null-energy consistency with macroscopic negative pressure.

papers.title: Learning from Duality in Neural Network Field Theories
papers.authors: Pietro Capuozzo, Brandon Robinson, Benjamin Suzzoni
papers.abstract: We develop neural realizations of positive-level Wess-Zumino-Witten models using bosonic Wakimoto and fermionic Fourier-Berezin fields. Level-rank duality connects the charged sectors of the fermionic construction, where explicit neural observables recover conformal block data and enable the transfer of information about unknown correlators between paired theories. We also show that distinct neural presentations of the same continuum current algebra exhibit different finite-width behavior, with approximation accuracy depending on architecture, regulator, and parameter distribution. These results connect the exact mathematical structure of conformal field theory with the expressive and computational properties of neural field theories.
papers.summary: The paper constructs neural network representations of positive-level Wess–Zumino–Witten models, using bosonic Wakimoto and fermionic Fourier–Berezin fields, and shows that level‑rank duality allows neural observables to recover conformal block data and transfer information between dual theories. It also demonstrates that different neural realizations of the same current algebra exhibit distinct finite‑width behaviors, linking the exact CFT structure to the expressive power of neural field theories.

papers.title: The Shape of the Strongly Coupled MQM Ground State
papers.abstract: We study a surprisingly efficient family of variational ansatze for the ground state of bosonic matrix quantum mechanics at large $N$. These are ansatze whose norm-squared probability distributions are themselves matrix integrals with single-trace actions, and so have their own independent `t Hooft expansions. They are efficient in the sense that optimizing over a small number of parameters produces many digits of accuracy for the energy, single-trace moments, and connected correlators. For infinite-$N$ planar data our results rapidly converge to within published bootstrap intervals and stabilize to a few digits of precision beyond them. We also demonstrate that we can efficiently capture $1/N$ corrections by computing connected two-point functions. These are matched against resummed quantum perturbation theory and Monte Carlo simulations.
papers.summary: This paper develops a compact variational ansatz for the ground state of large‑N bosonic matrix quantum mechanics, achieving high‑precision estimates of the energy, moments, and connected correlators with only a few parameters. The authors validate their approach against bootstrap bounds, resummed perturbation theory, and Monte Carlo data, and demonstrate systematic control of 1/N corrections.

papers.title: Self-interacting $p$-forms and the shear-free anisotropic cosmological model
papers.authors: Nicolas Hernandez (Universidad Industrial de Santander, Centro de Investigacion Cientifica y de Educacion Superior de Ensenada), Ben D. Normann (Norwegian University of Science and Technology), Yeinzon Rodriguez (Universidad Industrial de Santander, Universidad Antonio Narino)
papers.abstract: The cosmological principle may require more than observations demand: what is needed is isotropic expansion without vorticity. Extended Friedmann-Lemaitre-Robertson-Walker (eFLRW) cosmologies realise this with a non-vanishing anisotropic spatial curvature that is balanced by an anisotropic stress while the shear vanishes. Thorsrud and others investigated such scenarios for free differential $p$-forms. Here we extend the analysis to non-Abelian $p$-forms ($p=0,\dots,4$) with self interactions. The balance requires the anisotropic stress to decay as $a^{-2}$, $a$ being the cosmological scale factor, which we combine with the gauge-field continuity equation. The general results indicate that, in the presence of a potential, fine-tuning of the same is needed in order to balance the curvature.
